info.title: CV-CUE Web API Reference Guide
info.description:
# Introduction

The **CV-CUE Open API** is a set of HTTP REST APIs exposing all the functionality available via the
 CV-CUE (CloudVision Cognitive Unified Edge).

You can programmatically configure, manage, monitor, and troubleshoot your Wireless network and enables to
 integrate the CV-CUE Backend solution with your applications.

---

# Modules

All the resources served by the CV-CUE Backend are logically categorized in functionality based `modules`. Each
 module comprises resources that are functionally related to each other. A resource is a part of one module only.

Each module is versioned independently, giving us the flexibility to localise the version enhancements to only the
 changing modules while allowing other (non-impacting) modules to retain and support their respective versions for
 longer duration.
The module of a resource is the very first path parameter resource URI.

### CV-CUE Backend modules

- [session](/api/wm/session) - session related operations, like create a new session(authenticate) and delete a
 session (logout).
- [locations](/api/wm/locations) - all operations to fetch and manage the location hierarchy.
- [manageddevices](/api/wm/manageddevices) - operations to fetch and manage the Devices managed by the CV-CUE
 Backend.
- [aps](/api/wm/aps)- fetch and manage the Access Points managed and detected by the CV-CUE Backend.
- [clients](/api/wm/clients) - fetch and manage the Client devices associated and/or visible to the Managed
 Devices.
- [configuration](/api/wm/configuration) - comprises of all configuration policy related operations, like fetching
 or modifying a policy at any location.
- [deviceconfiguration](/api/wm/deviceconfiguration) - fetch and manage all kinds of Template and Profile
 configuration objects like Device Template, SSID Profile, Role Profile, etc.
- [troubleshooting](/api/wm/troubleshooting) - comprises of all the device troubleshooting related operations, like
 initiating a client connectivity test or a packet capture.
- [modules](/api/wm/modules) - fetch all the supported modules and their versions.

---

# API Versioning

As mentioned in the Modules section, CV-CUE Backend supports Module-based versioning which allows it to enhance
 each module independently.
The CV-CUE Backend increments the version of a particular module when,
- a new resource is introduced.
- a resource is deleted
- an existing resource is modified due to any of these reasons,
  + introduction of a new field
  + change in an existing field name or data type
  + deletion of an existing field
  + Change in validation rules of a field.

### Version in Header

The CV-CUE API call expects expects the Version number in the HTTP request-header `Version`.
The header if not specified, uses the request for the Latest supported version of the module.
A special value `latest` for this Version header is also supported to always serve the API for the latest supported
 version.

### API Deprecation

A Deprecated API call response will have a response header `Deprecated:Yes` set to help the API consumer identify
 the deprecated APIs.

---

# Error Codes

In all error cases, the CV-CUE API call responds with the appropriate 4XX or 5XX HTTP response code with a
 detailed information in the response body about the specific error whenever possible.
The error response typically contains a uniquely identifiable `errorcode`, a brief `message` about the error as
 well as `moreInfo` about the error.

---

# Accessing data in cluster/MSU deployment

As in non-cluster environments the data is accessible in the context of a `locationId`, in cluster/MSU deployments
, data is accessible in context of a combination of `nodeId` and `locationId`. The nodeId of the mounted child
 servers could be fetched from the location tree.

post.description: Create copy of the Device Template with the specified ID at the specified location. This also supports various options w.r.t. how overrides applicable to the source Device Template would apply to the newly created copy.

parameters.name: templateid
parameters.description: ID of the Device Template. Device Template IDs are system-generated. They can be obtained using [this API](../deviceconfiguration/8#/default/getAllDeviceTemplates).

parameters.name: nodeid
parameters.description: Node ID of the cluster node in cluster environment where the device template whose copy is to be created resides.

parameters.name: locationidtocopyoverriddenconfigfrom
parameters.description:
If set, the copy is not created using the original template definition, instead it is created using the resultant overridden template at the location denoted by this parameter. This parameter would be handy when one is looking to create a copy of the applicable template configuration at a certain location instead of the original template.

Please note that the parameter **keepoverriddenconfig** must not be set to **true** if using this parameter.

parameters.name: keepoverriddenconfig
parameters.description:
If the query param is set to true, then the applicable config for the new Device Template (at the common locations in the subtrees of the destination location and source Device Template creation location) would be same as that of the source Device Template. For the source Device Template, if there are overrides at the destination location and/or there are overrides getting inherited at the destination location, they would be patched to the new Device Template. All overrides associated with the source Device Template within the subtree of the destination location (except for the overrides at the destination location itself) would be copied to the new Device Template. If the query param is set to false, then the new Device Template would merely be a copy of the source Device Template, and would not have any overrides patched or associated to it.

Please note that the parameter **locationidtocopyoverriddenconfigfrom** must not be set if using this parameter.

post.description:
Create a session with the CV-CUE Backend server by authenticating using the appropriate mechanism, this is equivalent to logging in to the CV-CUE Backend service. 
CV-CUE Backend supports multiple authentication mechanisms for your applications to access the CV-CUE Backend APIs, these mechanisms are available based on the CV-CUE Backend deployment and usage. 

| Deployment Type|Usage                       |Authentication mechanism (`type`)|
|----------------|----------------------------|-----------------------------|
| Cloud 		 |Using the generated KeyId and KeyValue. This is a most common mechanism and to access APIs in **Cloud** deployed CV-CUE Backend servers. | APIKeyCredentials (`apikeycredentials`)|
| On-Premises     |Using the CV-CUE Backend local user's loginId and password. This is a most common mechanism and to access APIs in **On-Premises** deployed CV-CUE Backend servers. |UsernamePasswordCredentials (`usernamepasswordcredentials`)|
| On-Premises     |Using the configured RADIUS server in your local CV-CUE Backend server. |RadiusChallengeAnswer (`radiuschallengeanswer`)|
| On-Premises  |Using Certificate Authentication as per configurations in your local CV-CUE Backend server.| CertificateAuth (`certificateauth`)|

 On successful session creation, the  response header `Set-Cookie` has a cookie set (e.g `JSESSIONID=9AABA8048564822CB11FF7C0F3EC1B50`) which should be set as the `Cookie` header for all the subsequent requests made to the CV-CUE Backend server.

CACertificateChainPolicy.description: For AP to connect to CV-CUE Backend via IPsec tunnels, authentication would be done via custom x509 certificates. These custom certificates need to be signed by Certificate Authority. In such cases this policy would be used to manage these CA Certificates. Policy consists of all the CA Certificates available with CV-CUE Backend. Each CA Certificate is mapped to CA Certificate Chain Info object. There can be cases when the CA Certificates are chained, i.e. the CA certificate itself being signed by another CA, hence CA Certificate Chain Info object contains a set of CA Certificates which represents the chain of CA Certificates linked by IssuerDN to SubjectDN

priorityForTemplate.description: List containing all SSIDs enabled on the template, and their corresponding priority indices. The SSID profile with least index value has the highest priority. Each SSID profile should have unique priority index. The priority indices of SSID profiles are expected to be in a continuous range [1,n]. If API request does not provide continuous range of indices, during API processing the indices will be transformed to a continuous range [1,n].

priorityForRadios.description: A list of radio specific objects, where each object corresponds to SSID profiles enabled on the radio and their corresponding priority indices on the radio.

SSIDProfilesByPriority.description: Device Template SSID profile priority index object. The priority index is needed in case enabled SSID count across any of the bands exceeds 8. MFR platforms can support upto 14 SSIDs per band, while non-MFR platforms can support only upto 8 SSIDs. In case more than 8 SSIDs are enabled on a band, the top 8 SSIDs in priority across that band will be broadcasted on non-MFR platforms. On MFR platforms all SSIDs, irrespective of priority will be broadcasted.

radioId.description: ID of the radio corresponding to which priority indices for enabled SSIDs have been defined.

ssidProfilePriorityIndices.description: List containing SSID profiles IDs and corresponding priority indices. The priority indices of SSID profiles are unique and within a range [1,n].

SSIDProfilesPriorityOnRadio.description: Object containing radio ID and priority order of SSID Profiles enabled on corresponding radio. The priority indices of SSID profiles enabled on the radios are derived from the priority order on device template. The priority indices of SSID profiles at radio level is the condensed form of their priority order on device template. The condensed order is within a range [1,n]. On non-MFR platform APs, the SSID profiles having priority indices <= 8 are broadcasted on the corresponding radio. On MFR platform APs, all SSID profiles, irrespective of priority index are broadcasted on the radio.

recommendedAction.description: The recommended action to be taken if an event is raised by the system
recommendedAction.example: High utilization of AP means that the AP remains busy most of the time forwarding wireless traffic, and is indicative of capacity exhaustion. High AP utilization can result from one or more of: 1) High wireless traffic volume traversing the AP, 2) Low wireless transmission speeds which cause longer durations for wireless frames, 3) Excessive retransmissions. Depending upon the cause, corrective measures such as deploying more APs in areas of high capacity requirement, better placement and configuration of APs to increase wireless transmission speeds, reducing retransmissions by removing interference sources etc. can remedy this problem.

ServerAddressesInfo.description:
Represents server address info. The object of this class is used as a response  in the API to fetch CV-CUE Backend server addresses info. The response follows this order of priority:
 - **Access Address**: If the access address is set on the server, only access address will be set in the response.
 - **Cluster IP**: If the access address is not set and HA mode is enabled, the cluster IP (either IPv4 or IPv6) will be set in the response.
 - **Dual-Stack Mode**: If neither the access address nor the cluster IP is available, if CV-CUE Backend is running in dual-stack mode, both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses will be set in the response.
 - **Pure IPv4/IPv6 Mode**: Else either IPv4 or IPv6 address will be set in the response based on the mode.

interfaceName.description: The name of the network interface through which the ping packets should be sent. Default is bridge interface(br0), if not specified.

infinitePingEnabled.description: A flag to determine if the ping test should run indefinitely until manually stopped.

count.description: The number of ICMP echo requests to send. This limits the total number of packets sent during the test, unless infinitePingEnabled is set to true.

host.description: The destination IP address or hostname to ping.

ipVersion.description: The version of the Internet Protocol to use for the test (IPv4 or IPv6). This determines the format of the packets and the address type to be used.

packetSize.description: The size of the data payload in each ICMP packet, typically in bytes. Larger packets can be used to test for network fragmentation and performance under load.

dontFragment.description: A flag to set the Don't Fragment(DF) bit in the IP header of the packets. When true, packets that are too large to fit in a single frame are dropped by routers, which allows to test for the maximum transmission unit (MTU) along the network path.

intervalSeconds.description: The time delay in seconds between sending each ping packet.

destination.description: Destination hostname or IP address to which the route will be traced

maxHops.description: The maximum number of network hops (routers) the test will attempt to traverse. This field prevents the test from running indefinitely and is a crucial control mechanism for network diagnostics.

timeoutInSeconds.description: Timeout in seconds to wait for each probe response
